choice: orch health measures live: statvfs on the box, one df over SSH per probed device
why: the ticket names orch health; no new heartbeat table or poller thread, and self-heal already runs orch health every 2 minutes

choice: inode use at 85% or more, rounded up as df shows it; disk is reported, not alerted
why: the ticket asks for an inode alert; matching df's rounding means the alert agrees with what an operator sees in df

choice: the device's workdir_root; a missing one reads as unknown storage
why: job worktrees fill that filesystem, and the report names only a path df measured

choice: storage shows unknown with the df exit, no alert
why: reachability already has its own device-probe row; one failure should not be counted twice
the dashboard and orch status read the report often; an SSH round trip per device there would slow every refresh

choice: real orch health on the box: storage box / inodes 85% alert, pc 7%, exit 3, 0.5 s
why: matches df -i / (85%) at the same moment

choice: parse_df matches exactly as many value tokens as the header names between Filesystem and Mounted on, followed by an absolute mount path
why: right-aligning to the header broke when the mount name held spaces; both the filesystem and the mount name may hold spaces, but only the mount must start with /

choice: parse_df accepts a signed integer in every value column
why: GNU and BSD df print a negative Available on an over-full filesystem (102%); an unsigned pattern dropped the whole row and the disk read as unknown
